--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[EVT-1] Synchronous email send in public API
File: src/app/api/send/route.ts (L1-L250)
Evidence: The POST handler opens a nodemailer transporter and awaits transporter.sendMail(...) synchronously inside the HTTP request path with no queuing, rate limit, or idempotency checks. There is no recorded retry/backoff or dedupe store for sent messages.
Impact: A 10x spike will exhaust SMTP throughput or block serverless concurrency, causing request timeouts, large request backlogs, and duplicate emails if clients retry.  
Fix: Push email sends to a background queue/worker (or provider async webhook) and add an idempotency key or processed-events table to prevent duplicates.

[EVT-2] Synchronous WhatsApp API call without queuing or dedupe
File: src/app/api/whatsapp/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The POST handler directly calls the WhatsApp Business API (fetch to graph.facebook.com) and returns after awaiting the response, with no rate limiting, queuing, or idempotency on message IDs. Media upload logic is in-process and commented but would still be synchronous if enabled.
Impact: A 10x event spike will hit WhatsApp API rate limits and consume concurrency, causing failed requests, retries from clients, and duplicate messages due to repeated deliveries.  
Fix: Enqueue outgoing WhatsApp messages to a durable worker with retry/backoff and persist request IDs or idempotency tokens to avoid re-sends.

[EVT-3] Large-file uploads handled inline (no streaming/queue)
File: src/app/api/upload/route.ts (L1-L350)
Evidence: The POST handler reads full uploaded File into memory (file.arrayBuffer -> Buffer) and calls uploadToR2 synchronously; allowed sizes up to 500MB for videos with no chunking or async handoff. No concurrency limits, backpressure, or upload-worker offload exist.
Impact: A 10x spike of large uploads will exhaust memory and execution time for serverless instances, causing instance OOMs/timeouts, request backlog, and dropped uploads with no retry/DLQ

[EVT-2] Synchronous WhatsApp API call without queuing or dedupe
File: src/app/api/whatsapp/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The POST handler directly calls the WhatsApp Business API (fetch to graph.facebook.com) and returns after awaiting the response, with no rate limiting, queuing, or idempotency on message IDs. Media upload logic is in-process and commented but would still be synchronous if enabled.
Impact: A 10x event spike will hit WhatsApp API rate limits and consume concurrency, causing failed requests, retries from clients, and duplicate messages due to repeated deliveries.  
Fix: Enqueue outgoing WhatsApp messages to a durable worker with retry/backoff and persist request IDs or idempotency tokens to avoid re-sends.

[EVT-3] Large-file uploads handled inline (no streaming/queue)
File: src/app/api/upload/route.ts (L1-L350)
Evidence: The POST handler reads full uploaded File into memory (file.arrayBuffer -> Buffer) and calls uploadToR2 synchronously; allowed sizes up to 500MB for videos with no chunking or async handoff. No concurrency limits, backpressure, or upload-worker offload exist.
Impact: A 10x spike of large uploads will exhaust memory and execution time for serverless instances, causing instance OOMs/timeouts, request backlog, and dropped uploads with no retry/DLQ.  
Fix: Use direct client-to-storage uploads (presigned URLs) or stream/chunk uploads and offload processing to a queue/worker with size/ concurrency limits.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[EVT-4] Heavy synchronous export builds CSV in request
File: src/app/api/admin/orders/export/route.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: The POST handler fetches many orders and iterates to build a full CSV in-memory and returns it in the same request, with no pagination, rate limiting, or background job.  
Impact: Bulk export spikes (or many admin users) can cause DB contention and long-running requests that tie up workers, increasing latency for other APIs.  
Fix: Convert exports to an async job (generate CSV in background, store in R2/S3, notify when ready) or add pagination and concurrency limits.

[EVT-5] Admin abandoned-carts endpoint issues causing N+1 DB load
File: src/app/api/admin/abandoned-carts/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: The GET handler loads all partial checkouts then uses Promise.all to fetch carts and product details per cart, performing many sequential DB queries per item (possible N+1). No caching, batching, or job offload present.  
Impact: A burst of admin requests or large datasets will create DB spikes and slow responses, causing consumer lag and potential timeouts under 10x load.  
Fix: Batch queries with fewer joins (use single optimized query with includes), paginate results, and/or run heavy aggregation in background jobs.

--- INFO ---

[EVT-6] No queue/workflow library detected
File: package.json / repo dependencies
Evidence: package.json contains no queue/workflow libraries (no Bull/BullMQ/Temporal/Inngest/Trigger.dev/SQS/Kafka); async external calls are handled inline in API routes.
